evidence: Inspection of audit_report.md shows an English report title, five English finding titles, and English scope, conclusion, and conflict explanations. Chinese characters occur in the explicitly labeled Evidence bullets as source quotations; necessary party names are transliterated in the English prose.
observed: English title and substantive prose throughout; Chinese confined to cited evidence passages.
expected: The report title, every finding title, and substantive explanatory prose are English, with Chinese retained only as evidence, names, or necessary quoted terms.

requirement: Every reported finding must have a short English title, an explanation of the conflict, original Chinese evidence, and document-and-page location markers.
source_evidence: input/task_brief.md, lines 13-18: “For each finding, include: - a short English title; - a brief explanation of the conflict; - the original Chinese text that proves the issue; - a location marker with document name and page number.”
evidence: `grep -n '^## Finding' audit_report.md` identified five finding sections at lines 7, 17, 25, 33, and 45. Each has a nonempty English heading, a `Why it is inconsistent` explanation, and at least two compared Chinese evidence statements. Every evidence bullet carries a document and numeric page marker; where two quotations share a bullet, both are expressly attributed to the same document and page.
observed: 5 of 5 findings contain a title, explanation, multiple Chinese evidence statements, and document/page attributions.
expected: Every finding contains all four required components, and each evidence item has its own document-and-page attribution.

requirement: Each Chinese evidence quotation must actually occur on the cited page of the staged document.
source_evidence: input/task_brief.md, lines 15-18: “- the original Chinese text that proves the issue; - a location marker with document name and page number.” input/task_brief.md, line 23: “`input/extracted_text/` contains page-labeled UTF-8 text extracted from the PDFs for easier search.”
evidence: A reproducible comparison split each canonical extracted-text file at `=== Page N ===`, normalized Unicode width, whitespace, line wrapping, and standard punctuation, and tested the 21 quoted passages against their cited pages. Seventeen were contiguous matches, but four were not because the report inserted `……` between noncontiguous excerpts: (1) Finding 1, Announcement page 2, beginning `受让方2名称 厦门联芯美企业管理合伙企业（有限合伙）……`; (2) Finding 2, Announcement page 2, beginning `受让方1名称 杭州景祺电子信息合伙企业（有限合伙）……`; (3) Finding 2, Buyer 1 Report page 12, `四、本次权益变动的资金来源……本次权益变动资金来源部分来源于...`; and (4) Finding 5, Seller Report page 11, `信息披露义务人物美集团与杭州景祺签订了《股份转让协议》……信息披露义务人物美集团与厦门联芯美签订了《股份转让协议》……`. Those full quoted strings do not occur contiguously on the cited pages.
observed: 17 of 21 quoted passages are contiguous normalized page matches; 4 of 21 are noncontiguous composite quotations containing inserted ellipses.
expected: Every Chinese quotation must be a contiguous match on its cited document page after only the permitted normalization.
repair_hint: Split each of the four ellipsis-combined quotations into separately quoted, separately attributed contiguous excerpts from the same cited page; alternatively reproduce the intervening source text verbatim instead of inserting `……`.
